pages.title: hyponatremia — page 2
pages.status: 3 rows flagged — all 3 measured and all 3 confirmed. First of the described-only pages to be measured.
pages.lead: The work order gave no coordinate for any row on this page; every endpoint below was found by reading the artwork at 3-5x and confirmed by sampling the tissue under it with the leader's own ink excluded.

findings.label: Hypothalamus (osmoreceptors)
findings.now_desc: frontal-lobe cortical gyri, sampled (193,136,120). The leader is in TWO faint segments (ink peaks at x 105 and x 140) and both die in cortex
findings.target_desc: the gold hypothalamic nucleus at the top of the pituitary stalk, sampled (238,168,47) - unmistakable against anything around it

findings.label: Posterior Pituitary (stores & releases ADH)  [CHECK]
findings.now_desc: sampled (118,60,32), dark suprasellar tissue 12 px ABOVE the gland - the order is right that it stops short
findings.target_desc: the pinkish-brown pituitary teardrop at the foot of the stalk, sampled (166,91,77)

findings.label: Glomerulus
findings.now_desc: sampled (150,68,58) - the red arteriole entering from the left, OUTSIDE Bowman’s capsule
findings.target_desc: the bright red capillary tuft inside the capsule, sampled (184,85,68). Both arterioles are separately labelled on this panel, so the tuft is the only thing left unnamed

pages.note: Bowman’s Capsule on the same panel is CORRECT - its leader ends at (456,447) on the gold capsule ring, sampled (108,71,32). That matters for the fix: the Glomerulus leader has to reach past the capsule ring to the tuft inside it, so the two cannot simply be swapped end for end. ONE CORRECTION TO THE ORDER: it says the hypothalamic target is '~250px to the right'. Measured, it is 57 px (dx 53, dy 21). The direction and the target are right; the distance is not.

pages.title: bipolar — page 2
pages.status: 4 rows flagged — all 4 measured and all 4 confirmed, each endpoint carrying 37-56 px of leader ink.
pages.lead: A circuit diagram drawn over a midsagittal brain: coloured nodes joined by coloured pathway arcs, with white leaders running in from the numbered labels. Three of the four flagged leaders stop on a PATHWAY ARC rather than on the NODE the label names - the arcs are the conspicuous thing at that point on the page, and the leaders stop at the first one they meet.

findings.label: ⑤ HYPOTHALAMUS
findings.now_desc: sampled (123,99,127) - the purple GABA pathway arc, high and posterior in parietal white matter
findings.target_desc: the gold circuit node at the base of the diencephalon below the thalamus, sampled (172,135,39)

findings.label: ② ANTERIOR CINGULATE CORTEX
findings.now_desc: sampled (144,138,147) - the blue-tinted prefrontal band, well anterior to the cingulate
findings.target_desc: the cingulate gyrus immediately above the genu of the corpus callosum, sampled (204,167,149), where the orange arc runs

findings.label: ③ AMYGDALA  [CHECK]
findings.now_desc: sampled (107,176,148) - the GREEN PATHWAY ARC, not the node
findings.target_desc: the green amygdala sphere itself, sampled (118,186,112), 63 px to the right

findings.label: ④ BASAL GANGLIA  [CHECK]
findings.now_desc: sampled (96,77,77) - the pale corpus callosum at the upper margin of the deep-grey mass
findings.target_desc: inside the purple basal ganglia / thalamic mass, sampled (109,73,88)

pages.note: All four are short moves - 36 to 176 px - and none needs re-routing, because each label already approaches from the correct side. Row 3 is the cheapest and the clearest: 63 px along the leader's own axis, from the green arc onto the green sphere, both sampled and both unambiguous. ⑥ HIPPOCAMPUS and ⑦ BRAINSTEM were checked too and are not flagged here: ⑦ ends at (520,542) on the teal brainstem node, correct. ⑥'s leader ends at (617,523) on the CEREBELLUM, which is not the hippocampus - that row is NOT in the work order and needs the physician's read before we call it.

pages.title: b12-anemia — page 2
pages.panel: Labeled anatomy: vitamin B12 & folate absorption
pages.status: 4 rows flagged — all 4 endpoints measured; 3 targets measured, 1 needs placing from source.
pages.lead: No coordinate was given for any row on this page; every endpoint below was read off the artwork and confirmed by sampling the tissue under it. Three of the four faults are the same shape: a badge or leader stops on the DUODENAL/BOWEL tube it happens to overlie rather than on the organ its legend names.

findings.label: ③ marker — legend "Parietal Cells"
findings.now_desc: the badge sits on the pink DUODENAL C-LOOP at the pylorus, sampled (225,132,117) just under it
findings.target_desc: the gastric body/fundus where parietal cells actually sit, sampled (215,97,89)

findings.label: Pancreas  [CHECK]
findings.now_desc: the leader stops at the badge ③ ring on the pink duodenal wall - the orange pancreas does not begin until x≈455, so it is ~24 px short
findings.target_desc: the orange pancreas itself, sampled (196,120,65)

findings.label: ⑥ marker — legend "Transport" (B12 enters portal blood)  [CHECK]
findings.now_desc: sampled (112,52,48) - the pink BOWEL WALL. The leader runs left from the badge, curves up and dies on the gut
findings.target_desc: the blue portal vein drawn immediately to its left, sampled (22,69,119) - unmistakable against the bowel

findings.label: ⑤ Terminal ileum  [CHECK]
findings.now_desc: the badge sits on the bowel loop descending on the patient’s LEFT (the aorta/IVC pair run at x 430-467, so midline is ~455 and this loop is left of it)
findings.target_desc: the right lower quadrant, where the terminal ileum and cecum belong. PLACE FROM SOURCE - sampling the viewer-left lower quadrant returns background ((0,9,17) at (380,830)), so we could not find a distinctly drawn cecum to put a pixel on

pages.note: Row 1 has a second half the order flags and we confirm by absence: there is NO ④ marker anywhere on the figure, although the legend lists ④ Duodenum. So either the ③ badge is really the missing ④ sitting in the right place with the wrong number, or ④ was dropped. THAT CHANGES THE FIX - if it is a numbering error, renumber the badge rather than moving it, because it is already on the duodenum. Worth one look at the source file before anything is dragged. Rows 1, 2 and 4 are otherwise short, unambiguous moves.

pages.title: cirrhosis — page 2
pages.panel: Normal liver anatomy & portal venous system
pages.status: 4 rows flagged — 2 measured and confirmed (main figure); rows 3 and 4 are on other panels and are NOT yet measured.
pages.lead: The main figure draws the falciform ligament as a narrow pale cream band. Measured at the leaders' own row it spans only x 590-597 - about 8 px - which is the whole difficulty: both flagged leaders overshoot it into liver parenchyma.

findings.label: Falciform ligament
findings.now_desc: ink 24 confirms a real terminator; tissue (139,100,93), left-lobe parenchyma, 35 px lateral to the band
findings.target_desc: the cream band itself, sampled (207,161,125) at x 590-597

findings.label: Ligamentum teres (round ligament)
findings.now_desc: ink 19; tissue (55,35,31), the shadowed inferolateral margin of the left lobe
findings.target_desc: the cream cord descending below the liver from the falciform, sampled (199,155,122) through y 428-468

pages.note: ONE CORRECTION TO THE ORDER'S MAGNITUDES, same as on hyponatremia: it puts row 1 at '~160px lateral to the midline' and row 2 at '~145px'. Measured, row 1 is 35 px from the band. The finding is right, the distance is not - do not drag by the order's numbers. ROWS 3 AND 4 ARE NOT MEASURED: row 3 Xiphoid process is in the SURFACE LANDMARKS panel and row 4 Diaphragm is in PERITONEAL RELATIONSHIPS. They are carried at the order's wording until the next pass.

pages.title: covid — page 2
pages.status: 4 rows flagged — 3 measured and confirmed (legend leaders on the main figure); row 2 is in the epithelium panel and is NOT yet measured.
pages.lead: Three of the four are LEGEND leaders - the lines running from the numbered list on the left across to the figure. Two of them never arrive: they stop in the black background outside the facial silhouette. The on-figure badges themselves are correctly placed, which is what makes this survive a skim - the reader sees a numbered badge in the right place and does not notice that the legend line beside it points at nothing.

findings.label: ② Nasopharynx (legend leader)  [CHECK]
findings.now_desc: sampled (2,4,10) - near-black EMPTY BACKGROUND just outside the facial silhouette, near the nose/upper lip
findings.target_desc: the airway behind the nasal cavity, sampled (60,99,117), where the on-figure badge ② already sits correctly

findings.label: ③ Oropharynx (legend leader)  [CHECK]
findings.now_desc: sampled (13,15,20) - near-black EMPTY BACKGROUND at the chin/submental outline
findings.target_desc: the pharyngeal airway behind the tongue, sampled (71,65,93)

findings.label: ④ Larynx (legend leader)
findings.now_desc: a horizontal leader at y≈575 running right across the whole neck and dying on the TRACHEA, just below the ⑤ Trachea badge at (365,560)
findings.target_desc: the pale laryngeal cartilage below the epiglottis, sampled (242,165,166)

pages.note: MEASURED CAVEAT on row 1: the ink run at y 575 is continuous from x 240 to about x 360, but the trachea's own pale rings also register there, so the terminus is given as ≈(358,575) rather than to the pixel. The finding - that it ends on trachea rather than larynx - does not depend on that precision. ROW 2 NOT MEASURED: Basal Cell is in the RESPIRATORY EPITHELIUM panel (page x 478-990, y 990-1143); the order has it on the stalk of the purple goblet cell when it belongs on the squat cuboidal row at the basement membrane. Carried at the order's wording. PANELS SWEPT: the main figure's badges ①-⑧ were checked and all sit on their structures - it is only the legend LINES that fail.

pages.title: croup — page 2
pages.lead: Orientation first: the child faces LEFT (nose tip ~(278,415)) and the vertebral bodies run down x 445-475, so anterior is left and posterior is right. Every one of the four defects is a leader that OVERSHOOTS its structure along its own line of travel and stops in the tissue beyond — the Epiglottis leader crosses the pale epiglottic leaf and halts 12px posterior to it in the laryngeal vestibule, the Vocal cords leader carries on past the glottic level and lands inside the yellow dashed Subglottic-space callout box, and the Trachea leader runs the full width of the figure past the trachea and carina to end in lung parenchyma. Oral cavity is the odd one: it stops dead at the closed lips on the face surface and then resumes as two detached dotted stubs on the tongue.

findings.label: Trachea
findings.now_desc: sampled (64,45,49) - dark maroon lung parenchyma in the viewer's-left lung field, 150px below the carina at ~(400,755)
findings.target_desc: the ringed blue-grey trachea between larynx and carina (column x 400-435), sampled (147,168,197)

findings.label: Vocal cords
findings.now_desc: sampled (137,63,61) - dark red tissue INSIDE the yellow dashed Subglottic space callout box, whose bounds I measured as x 394-437, y 546-587
findings.target_desc: PLACE FROM SOURCE - no vocal-cord structure is drawn. At 22x the airway column between the epiglottic tip and the box's top edge (x 400-435, y 528-546) is undifferentiated dark red with only a blurred fold at x 419-424; the glottic LEVEL is identifiable but there is no glyph to land on, and picking a pixel would be inventing one

findings.label: Epiglottis
findings.now_desc: sampled (150,78,83) - dark red laryngeal vestibule 12px posterior to the epiglottis; the leader crosses the pale leaf (which spans x 391-400 at y=532) and overshoots it
findings.target_desc: the pale leaf-shaped epiglottis itself, sampled (187,167,171)

findings.label: Oral cavity
findings.now_desc: sampled (90,42,39) - the lip/nasolabial shadow at the closed mouth on the face surface; ink trace dies at x=292 and the leader then RESUMES as two detached dotted stubs ending on the tongue body at (334,461) and (333,492)
findings.target_desc: the dark oral airspace between the hard palate above and the tongue dorsum below, sampled (95,32,32)

pages.note: Panels swept: main sagittal figure, ANATOMY COMPARISON (child vs adult larynx: Epiglottis/Vocal cords/Subglottic space/Trachea all land correctly on both figures), CROSS-SECTION, AIRFLOW AND RESISTANCE, WHY KIDS GET CROUP (Cricoid cartilage). No defect beyond the four flagged. Nothing carried unmeasured. The Vocal cords target is the only null and the reason is stated above.

pages.title: gi-bleed — page 2
pages.panel: Upper GI Anatomy: Structures at Risk for Bleeding
pages.lead: Handedness: the liver is drawn at viewer-left, so viewer-left is the patient's RIGHT, which puts the fundus dome (viewer-right of the oesophagus) on the patient's left - anatomically correct, and it means the three stomach-region defects are not a mirroring problem. They are a one-step SHIFT ALONG THE GREATER CURVATURE: Cardia sits where Fundus belongs (top of the dome), Fundus sits where upper Body belongs, and Antrum sits at the lower body 176px from the pylorus, which in this drawing is at the LEFT where the duodenal bulb begins. All three dots land on the same pale outer-wall band, so the error is purely positional. Serosa is unrelated - a one-layer undershoot on the block's shaded right face.

findings.label: Cardia
findings.now_desc: sampled (185,114,101) - the pale outer wall of the fundus dome at its top-right, 92px right and 28px above the oesophagogastric junction
findings.target_desc: the EG junction notch where the oesophagus opens into the stomach, sampled (210,120,104)

findings.label: Fundus
findings.now_desc: sampled (173,97,90) - greater-curvature wall 72px BELOW the Cardia dot, i.e. upper body not dome
findings.target_desc: the apex of the dome above the cardia, on the same pale wall band the other three dots use, sampled (~205,110,95)

findings.label: Antrum
findings.now_desc: sampled (204,126,111) - mucosal folds of the lower body near the greater curvature; I measured the pylorus/duodenal junction at ~(243,545), so this is 176px from it
findings.target_desc: the distal stomach lumen just proximal to the pylorus, at the drawing's LEFT where the duodenal bulb begins, sampled (130,31,19)

findings.label: Serosa / Adventitia
findings.now_desc: sampled (86,37,34) - the outer longitudinal muscle band on the block's shaded right face. Vertical profile at x=267: pale intramuscular septum y 1130-1144, muscle y 1146-1172, blue subserosal vessel y 1176-1180, serosa y 1182-1196, block edge y 1198. The dot sits in the muscle band
findings.target_desc: the outermost serosal layer BELOW the blue subserosal vessel on the same right face, sampled (94,45,47) - dark only because that face is shaded; its hue is rosy (g~=b) against the muscle's strong red (b<<g)

pages.note: Panels swept: main stomach figure (Oesophagus dot (358,311) and Ligament of Treitz dot (377,693) both correct), WALL ANATOMY block (Mucosa (271,940), Submucosa (268,1018), Muscularis Externa (269,1084) all correct), THE LIGAMENT OF TREITZ, ARTERIAL SUPPLY and KEY ANATOMIC RELATIONSHIPS (text only). No defect beyond the four flagged.

pages.title: myasthenia — page 2
pages.panel: Normal Neuromuscular Junction (Labeled Neuromuscular Junction Anatomy)
pages.lead: Three of the four are leaders that stop in the nearest BULK COMPARTMENT instead of on the thin structure they name: Basal lamina lands 58px deep in striated sarcoplasm rather than on the fold surface, Voltage-gated Ca2+ channels lands 23px inside the terminal's cytoplasm rather than in the bright membrane band at x 214-222, and ACh release lands 12px outside the terminal in plain black background. The fourth is different and is a genuine mislabel: AChR is drawn as TWO leaders, and while the lower one correctly reaches a blue receptor, the upper one passes straight over that same receptor and terminates on an orange ACh molecule.

findings.label: Basal lamina
findings.now_desc: sampled (164,92,104) - striated sarcoplasm inside the muscle fibre; measured 58px below the junctional-fold bases (~y 703) and 41px above the Muscle fiber dot at (234,802)
findings.target_desc: the thin pale layer lining the synaptic surface of the junctional folds, sampled (211,132,147)

findings.label: Voltage-gated Ca2+ channels
findings.now_desc: sampled (46,35,51) - presynaptic cytoplasm; the horizontal profile at y=474 puts the bright membrane band at x 214-222, so the arrowhead tip is 23px inside it. No channel glyph is drawn at the endpoint
findings.target_desc: the presynaptic membrane band itself, sampled (99,78,150)

findings.label: Acetylcholine (ACh) release
findings.now_desc: sampled (13,19,23) - plain black background 12px outside the terminal's lower-left edge, on no vesicle and no ACh sphere
findings.target_desc: a released orange ACh sphere in the synaptic cleft, sampled (237,180,74); the fusing vesicle at the terminal's base (256,511) is the alternative

findings.label: Acetylcholine receptors (nicotinic, AChR) — UPPER leader
findings.now_desc: sampled (202,156,110) at the sphere centre (246,581) - an orange ACh molecule. The leader runs at y 581-583 straight over the blue receptor at x 204-232 and stops on the sphere at x 240-250
findings.target_desc: the body of the blue receptor glyph the leader already crosses, sampled (105,129,192)

pages.note: Panels swept: Normal NMJ (all 10 leaders), OVERVIEW, SINGLE JUNCTION (CROSS-SECTION), KEY MOLECULES, HOW NEUROMUSCULAR TRANSMISSION WORKS (5 steps), IN MYASTHENIA GRAVIS. The LOWER of the two AChR leaders ends at (216,599), sampled (71,98,156) - on a blue receptor stem, correct, leave it. One borderline item the order did not list and I am not raising as a finding: the Postsynaptic membrane dot at (252,703) sits ~13px below the basal turn of the fold above it rather than on the fold lining, but the pale lining band does pass through that point, so it is defensible as drawn.

pages.title: sickle-cell — page 2
pages.lead: The spleen panel's six leaders all arrive as horizontal rules at fixed rows (y 367/416/473/529/594/640) and simply stop at whatever x the layout gave them, which is how three of them go wrong: Trabeculae stops 12px past the upper follicle in red pulp with no trabecular band anywhere on the organ, Red pulp stops at x=850 - the same x as the White pulp rule one row above at x=851 - so the two are visually indistinguishable and Red pulp reads as naming the follicle it is touching, and Splenic vein doglegs UP off its rule onto the pink capsule instead of reaching the blue vein 33px to its left. The two microvasculature leaders are vertical and both OVERSHOOT the vessel wall into the lumen, each stopping on a red cell 10-20px past the structure named.

findings.label: Trabeculae
findings.now_desc: sampled (66,32,60) at (830,416) - dark red pulp 12px right of the upper white-pulp follicle, whose right margin I measured at x=819
findings.target_desc: PLACE FROM SOURCE - no trabecular band is drawn anywhere in this spleen. At 8-14x the parenchyma is swirling mauve reticular texture only; the sole pale fibrous structures are the segmented capsule blocks at the rim, and calling one of those a trabecula would be inventing the target

findings.label: Red pulp (filters blood)
findings.now_desc: sampled (64,31,58) at (848,529) - the shadowed rim of the lower follicle, 13px past its lavender margin at x=837. The White pulp rule above ends at x=851, so the two terminate at the same x and read identically
findings.target_desc: the dark red inter-follicular parenchyma that fills most of the organ, sampled (58,13,32) - note the hue, strongly red (b<<r), against the follicle's purple (b>=r)

findings.label: Splenic vein
findings.now_desc: sampled (132,74,104) at (806,631) - the pink capsule at the spleen's inferomedial corner. The rule runs in at y=640 to x=803 then doglegs UP to a bright tip at (803,634), away from the vessels
findings.target_desc: the blue splenic vein 33px to its left at the same height, sampled (15,60,117) - the way Splenic artery reaches its red branch

findings.label: Endothelium
findings.now_desc: sampled (65,15,16) - a dark red blood cell in the lumen; the leader crosses the pale lining at y~858-864 and runs 20px past it (ink trace: solid to y=881, gone by y=884)
findings.target_desc: the pale endothelial lining band itself, sampled (184,102,97)

findings.label: Adhesion molecules
findings.now_desc: sampled (125,39,40) - a bright red blood cell in the lumen, 10px below the wall band (which at x=441 runs y 864-876)
findings.target_desc: the dark wall-bound adhesion molecule at x 445-453, y 869-876 that the leader passes on its way down, sampled (54,18,18)

pages.note: Panels swept: SPLEEN (all six), MICROVASCULATURE & ISCHEMIA (three), HEMOGLOBIN, RED BLOOD CELLS, SICKLE MUTATION, HEMOLYSIS, MAJOR ORGANS, THE SICKLE PROCESS. One near-miss I chased and cleared: the Splenic artery rule appears to end on the blue vein at (770,599), but that bright pixel is a SPECULAR HIGHLIGHT on the vein, not leader ink - the rule itself runs at y=594 and ends at (796,594) beside a red arterial branch entering the hilum. Correct as drawn. I only believed that after a row-by-row RGB scan; by eye at 24x it reads as a defect.

pages.title: thrombocytopenia — page 2
pages.status: 5 rows flagged — 5 measured and confirmed (1 target null, with the reason established from the page's own legend)
pages.lead: In the marrow panel the two leaders have SWAPPED what they touch: Sinusoid crosses the blue vessel it names and carries 26px past it onto a purple megakaryocyte pseudopod, while Proplatelet extensions stops on the sinusoid's dark blue right wall with no purple process within ~28px. In the platelet panel the mechanism is different and is settled by the page's own KEY PLATELET COMPONENTS legend, which colour-codes dense granules ORANGE (dot (876,1204), rgb (253,184,44)) and lysosomes YELLOW-GREEN (dot (873,1268), rgb (205,222,144)). The platelet contains exactly two orange-cored granules and both are UNLABELLED, while the Dense granule and Lysosome leaders converge on one and the same blue-teal granule from opposite sides. No granule in the platelet is yellow-green at all.

findings.label: Sinusoid (marrow capillary)
findings.now_desc: sampled (114,82,143) - a lavender megakaryocyte pseudopod. Ink trace: the leader doglegs, crosses the blue sinusoid at ~(486,582), then runs down-left to a tip at (467,600), 26px past the crossing
findings.target_desc: the blue sinusoid at the point the leader already crosses it, sampled (71,98,144)

findings.label: Proplatelet extensions into sinusoid
findings.now_desc: sampled (61,82,117) - the dark blue shadowed right wall of the sinusoid, not red marrow as the order estimated and not a purple process; the hue is unambiguous (g>r, b>>r). Nearest proplatelet ~28px to the left
findings.target_desc: a purple proplatelet strand where it meets the sinusoid's upper margin, sampled (126,84,145)

findings.label: Lysosome (hydrolytic enzymes)
findings.now_desc: sampled (74,63,118) - the lower-left border of the blue-teal granule at 3 o'clock (granule spans x 798-818, y 405-433), the same granule the Dense granule leader is aimed at from the right
findings.target_desc: PLACE FROM SOURCE - the legend's lysosome swatch is yellow-green (205,222,144) and NO granule in the platelet is that colour; the two leaders cannot both own the blue-teal granule, and choosing which glyph becomes the lysosome is a source decision, not something the artwork answers

findings.label: Dense granule (ADP, ATP, Ca2+, serotonin)
findings.now_desc: sampled (77,58,109) - plain purple cytoplasm at the base of a pseudopod, 5px right of the blue-teal granule's edge at x=818
findings.target_desc: the nearer of the two unlabelled orange-cored granules, sampled (229,169,92) - the legend colour-codes dense granules orange (253,184,44); the second orange granule is at (750,429), sampled (230,153,94)

findings.label: Open canalicular system
findings.now_desc: sampled (12,14,24) - black background outside the cell, 4px beyond the upper-right pseudopod bulb (bulb centre (828,314), halo edge x~837, sampled (171,135,195))
findings.target_desc: a pale tubular channel of the internal network drawn inside the platelet body, sampled (178,149,209)

pages.note: Panels swept: MEGAKARYOPOIESIS (Bone trabecula, Bone marrow, Megakaryocyte, Sinusoid, Proplatelet extensions, Platelets entering circulation, and the five numbered stem-cell steps), PLATELET STRUCTURE (all five), PLATELETS IN CIRCULATION, THE SPLEEN, PLATELETS: ROLE IN PRIMARY HEMOSTASIS (5 steps), KEY PLATELET COMPONENTS. Found beyond the order: the legend/artwork colour mismatch described in the lead - it is what makes finding 4 pinnable and finding 3 not, and it is worth telling production that no yellow-green lysosome glyph exists. Nothing carried unmeasured.
